analysis:
The only change in this PR is a documentation addition to docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1030-1047). It describes a new PromptTokenCache in LocalTokenizerBridge. The cache reuses token IDs for rendered-prompt pieces within the same prefix-cache scope. It also adds ChatTemplateLoopRewrites, which are linear-time Gemma 4 and GPT-OSS template renderers, plus a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_PROMPT_CACHE=0 kill switch. No code is in the supplied evidence, so this is a documentation claim only and not a verified implementation.

Security-relevant claims I examined against T-041, SEC-035 and A-001:
1. The doc says reuse never crosses a cache scope. That matches the coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping, so cross-account reuse is not described as possible.
2. The prompt-piece cache is in-process only (no on-disk artifact is described), so T-041's at-rest leak #2 mitigations are not affected by this text.
3. It adds a possible same-scope timing signal: pieces seen before encode faster. That is a render and tokenization latency difference, separate from the TTFT KV-hit oracle. It stays within the same-account scope already accepted under SEC-035. The doc does not describe the lifetime, size bounds or eviction of the cache of plaintext-derived token IDs held in memory.
4. The doc claims ID equivalence with applyChatTemplate, backed by sampled background comparisons that disable reuse on a mismatch. The comparison logic is not visible here.
5. The doc says new long prompts encode on up to four cores. That could add availability pressure for adversarial consumers if concurrency is not bounded. This is unverified.

No concrete regression is supported by the visible text. The integration questions for the code review are these: how the scope key is derived and enforced in PromptTokenCache; its memory bounds and lifetime; and whether the cached plaintext-derived data is cleared on model unload (T-028, T-011).
